coalitions.name: New Hampshire Network for Environment, Energy, and Climate
coalitions.description: Volunteer-run network founded in January 2021 that brings together about 30 New Hampshire environment, energy and climate groups, with working groups, monthly webinars and an annual summit.

projects.name: Monthly webinar and working-group series
projects.description: Recorded webinars on climate science, offshore wind, plastics, nuclear energy and forest policy, plus Climate, Energy, Plastics and Environment working groups.

actions.name: Work through the NH Network take-action list
actions.description: Ongoing actions include contacting legislators on climate and energy bills, supporting plastic bag reduction and Carbon Cash-Back advocacy.

coalitions.name: Community Power Coalition of New Hampshire
coalitions.description: Nonprofit joint powers agency, incorporated in 2021, through which New Hampshire municipalities and counties run community power electricity programs, group net metering and related clean-energy services. Roughly 64 municipalities and 4 counties are members; 40 are listed here.

projects.name: PEAK SHAVE and group net metering programs
projects.description: Member services including a demand-management program, renewable energy certificate aggregation and group net metering for municipalities.

coalitions.name: New Hampshire Coastal Adaptation Workgroup
coalitions.description: Collaboration of more than 40 agencies, municipalities, universities, non-profits and firms helping New Hampshire's coastal communities adapt to climate change, with workshops, summits and the Picturing Rising Tides photo project. Design and engineering firm members are not listed here.

events.name: Picturing Rising Tides 2026 photo submission window
events.description: Annual community photo project documenting high tides and flooding on the New Hampshire coast; photos are submitted Oct 26 to Nov 3.

coalitions.name: Granite State Clean Cities Coalition
coalitions.description: US Department of Energy Clean Cities coalition coordinated by NH DES, with 150+ stakeholders from transit, fleets, fuel providers, EV charging firms, universities and government working to cut petroleum use in transportation. Only public-sector, transit, university and utility stakeholders are listed here.

coalitions.name: New Hampshire Association of Conservation Commissions
coalitions.description: Nonprofit founded in 1970 that supports and represents more than 200 municipal conservation commissions through training, regional events and legislative advocacy. Individual member commissions are not published as a list.

coalitions.name: Carbon Cash-Back Coalition
coalitions.description: Grassroots New Hampshire coalition advocating a carbon fee with dividends returned to residents; its steering committee draws on Pemi Climate Emergency Coalition, Citizens' Climate Lobby, 350NH and League of Conservation Voters volunteers.

coalitions.name: Local Energy Solutions (LES) New Hampshire
coalitions.description: Clean Energy NH work group, formed in 2011, that gives technical support and training to local energy committees, municipalities and schools; participants include energy professionals, municipal volunteers and agencies such as EPA New England and NH DES. notes: WebFetch worked for most sites; cleanenergynh.org/members, nhcaw.org home, nhacc and some others were fetched only via specific pages; a few fetches failed (permission/robots: Climate Action NH Facebook, newhampshirenetwork.org home, nhsea.org, nhcoastaladaptation.org). No work-around used. Candidates not found as real coalitions: 'Climate Action NH' (only a Facebook page seen, robots-blocked), NH Healthy Homes/Healthy Kids, NH Rivers Council (not checked as coalition), a NH Environmental Common Agenda equivalent or Environmental Lobby Day (none found), NH Youth Climate coalition (only a 2020 one-off town hall), Seacoast area climate partner coalition (Seacoast Climate Action NOW is a single volunteer nonprofit, not in this file). NHSEA is the former name of Clean Energy NH (same org), so it is one org, not a coalition. Clean Energy NH publishes ~100 mostly business members (all-members page) but is a trade association, so it is an org here with no member edges. Monadnock Sustainability Hub is treated as an org, not a coalition (lists 5 partners: Clean Energy NH, Sierra Club, Monadnock Food Co-op, Cheshire County Conservation District, Hannah Grimes Center; not added as members). Coalitions without member lists: NHACC (200+ town conservation commissions unlisted), LES work group (no roster). CPCNH: capped at 40 of ~51 listed member programs (3 counties + first 37 towns on the members page); omitted: Charlestown, Durham, Franconia, Hanover, Kensington, Lyme, New London, Peterborough, Rye, Sugar Hill, Walpole (the site also says 64 municipalities and 4 counties as of May 2025, so the list is not complete). CAW: omitted ~14 design/engineering firms and BeachGoods.com, plus unclear 'UNH Climate & Interior Climate Adaptation Center' and 'Seacoast Watershed Commission'. GSCCC: 150+ stakeholders, only transit, universities, state agencies and Eversource listed. NH Network: the About page lists 29 organizations (it says about 30); 'League of Conservation Voters' assumed to be NH LCV; WindowDressers is Maine-based; Carbon Cash-Back Coalition is itself a coalition (linked as nh_carbon_cash_back_coalition_c). The NH Network 5th summit was Sept 26 per its events page (a news story says Sept 28) and is past. Locations for most volunteer groups are state-capital placeholders (remote true or approx) since no address was published; websites left empty where not verified. Coalition last_activity for CAW left blank (2026 summit recap exists but date not read). CPCNH last_activity 2026-05-08 is the NH Energy Week 2026 end date. NH Healthy Climate Nov 18 event year assumed 2026 from the host's chronological list.
